criteria.text: Routes are checked in the order they were registered.
The first route that returns a full match handles the request and the search stops.
A partial match (path matches, method does not) is only used when no full match is found.
A request that matches no route falls through to a 404 via the default handler.
Routes are ranked by path specificity or longest matching prefix.
The router collects every matching route and then picks the best one.

ServerErrorMiddleware is the outermost middleware and turns otherwise-unhandled errors into 500s.
ServerErrorMiddleware re-raises the exception after sending its response.
ExceptionMiddleware maps HTTPException and registered handlers to responses without re-raising.
ExceptionMiddleware is installed innermost, closest to the router.
Because ExceptionMiddleware is inside user middleware, it does not catch errors raised by user middleware.
ExceptionMiddleware is the outermost middleware and the first to see a request.

criteria.text: The endpoint invocation is wrapped by wrap_app_handling_exceptions.
For an HTTPException the wrapper checks a status-code handler before a class-based handler.
The class-based handler lookup walks the exception type's MRO.
If no handler is found the exception is re-raised.
If the response has already started, a RuntimeError is raised instead of handling.
Route.handle itself contains the try/except that converts the exception.
The exception propagates to ServerErrorMiddleware, which renders the HTTPException as its response.

criteria.text: Today ExceptionMiddleware sits closest to the router and does not see exceptions raised by user middleware.
After the move, exceptions raised in user middleware would be caught by ExceptionMiddleware.
An HTTPException raised in user middleware would then render as its mapped response instead of a 500.
ServerErrorMiddleware remains the outermost layer and still handles otherwise-unhandled errors.
Registered class or status-code exception handlers behave the same either way.
The change would let ExceptionMiddleware catch errors raised by ServerErrorMiddleware too.
Moving ExceptionMiddleware changes how the router matches routes or dispatches endpoints.
